findings.claim: The rate of decomposition depends on several factors (B4.2b).
findings.truth: There is no statement B4.2b in this qualification. Topic B4 has one section only, B4.1 Ecosystems (B4.1a-f). Decomposition sits under B4.1b. Rate of decomposition is not itself a numbered statement, so the code is removed rather than swapped.
findings.evidence: spec bold file, Topic B4: only B4.1 Ecosystems is listed; grep for B4.2 returns nothing in either spec file

findings.claim: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria ... convert atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia and then into nitrates
findings.truth: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria convert nitrogen gas to ammonia. Nitrifying bacteria are the group that converts ammonia to nitrite and then nitrate. The sentence credits one group with both steps.
findings.evidence: settled biology; the two bacterial groups are distinct

findings.claim: CO_2 in four flashcard answers ([0], [1], [2], [11])
findings.truth: Flashcard fields are plain text and must use the unicode subscript, so the student sees CO2 with a real subscript rather than raw LaTeX.
findings.evidence: house rule: *_html fields use entities, plain-text fields use unicode

findings.claim: Individual \to population \to community \to ecosystem.
findings.truth: Raw LaTeX \to leaks into a plain-text flashcard answer. Use the unicode arrow.
findings.evidence: house rule: plain-text fields use unicode

findings.claim: Four wrong statement codes: haploid/diploid cited as (B5.1b), the genetic terms as (B5.1c), Punnett squares as (B5.1d), sex determination as (B5.1e).
findings.truth: In this specification B5.1a is the list of genetic terms, B5.1b is the genome, B5.1d is mutations and variants, B5.1e is haploid and diploid, B5.1h is Punnett squares and B5.1i is sex determination. Each citation is shifted, so a student who looks a code up lands on the wrong statement.
findings.evidence: spec B5.1 Inheritance statement table (identical in the v4.3 and v5.0 extractions)

findings.claim: What is the genotype of a heterozygous individual? Options BB / bb / Bb / bB, correct = Bb.
findings.truth: bB is the same genotype as Bb, so the question has two correct answers and marks a correct student wrong. Option [3] is replaced with a distractor that is not heterozygous.
findings.evidence: settled genetics: allele order in a genotype carries no meaning

findings.claim: What phenotypic ratio does Bb \times Bb produce?
findings.truth: Raw LaTeX \times in a plain-text flashcard question. Use the unicode multiplication sign.
findings.evidence: house rule: plain-text fields use unicode

findings.claim: OCR Gateway 'discuss' questions (8 marks) on evolution
findings.truth: There is no 8-mark question on these papers. Each biology paper is 60 marks in two sections: Section A multiple choice worth 10 marks, Section B worth 50 marks containing short-answer styles and one extended six-mark Level of Response question.
findings.evidence: spec assessment section: 'extended six-mark Level of Response question'; Paper 2 / Paper 8 are 60 marks, 1 hour 10 minutes

findings.claim: OCR Gateway 'discuss' questions (8 marks) on human impacts
findings.truth: Same fault as F8: the highest tariff is the extended six-mark Level of Response question.
findings.evidence: spec assessment section for Paper 2 and Paper 8

findings.claim: OCR Gateway 'discuss' questions (8 marks) on food production
findings.truth: Same fault as F8: the highest tariff is the extended six-mark Level of Response question.
findings.evidence: spec assessment section for Paper 2 and Paper 8

findings.claim: Natural selection cited as (B5.2b), speciation as (B5.2c), evidence for evolution as (B5.2d), selective breeding as (B5.2f).
findings.truth: B5.2b is classification systems, B5.2c is how evolution occurs by natural selection, B5.2d is evolution and the formation of new species, B5.2e is the evidence for evolution. B5.2f does not exist: B5.2 runs a to e. Selective breeding is B6.2a.
findings.evidence: spec B5.2 and B6.2 statement tables

findings.claim: Mark scheme point: 'Natural selection increases genetic variation over time, selective breeding reduces it'.
findings.truth: Natural selection does not increase genetic variation. Mutation is the source of new variation; selection acts on variation that already exists and generally narrows it. The comparison point is rewritten so selective breeding reduces variation because few parents are chosen.
findings.evidence: settled biology; spec B5.2c ties natural selection to the concept of mutation as the source of variants

findings.claim: The OCR Gateway specification also requires understanding of eutrophication in detail.
findings.truth: Eutrophication is not named anywhere in this specification. The process is fine to teach as an example of a negative human interaction (B6.1b), but the claim about what the specification requires is false.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec: no match for 'eutroph'

findings.claim: Indicator species cited as (B6.1c); sustainability and conservation cited as (B6.1d).
findings.truth: B6.1 runs a to c only, so B6.1d does not exist. The lichen pollution work sits under B6.1b, and conservation schemes, ecotourism and the benefits and challenges of biodiversity are B6.1c.
findings.evidence: spec B6.1 statement table and its practical suggestions column

findings.claim: Biological control ... may become an invasive species or fail to control the pest effectively (B6.2c).
findings.truth: B6.2c is the main steps of genetic engineering, and it is bold in the specification, so Higher Tier only. Biological control is not in this specification at all. The code is removed.
findings.evidence: spec bold file B6.2c; grep of the spec: no match for 'biological control'

findings.claim: The OCR Gateway specification also expects you to understand the concept of food miles.
findings.truth: Food miles are not in this specification. The paragraph can stay as background, but the claim about what the specification expects is false.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec: no match for 'food mile'

findings.claim: Three practice questions and four of the five knowledge checks test restriction enzymes, sticky ends, ligase, plasmid vectors and antibiotic resistance markers with no tier flag, in a lesson whose tier is 'both'.
findings.truth: B6.2c ('describe the main steps in the process of genetic engineering', with restriction enzymes, sticky ends, ligase, host bacteria, antibiotic resistance markers and vectors) is the only bold statement in B4-B6, so it is Higher Tier only. Practice [0], [3] and [5] and knowledge checks [0], [2], [3] and [4] now carry a '(Higher tier)' prefix.
findings.evidence: spec bold file: B6.2c and its whole 'to include' column are bold; the tiering note says bold statements are tested in Higher Tier papers only

findings.claim: golden rice has been modified to produce beta-carotene (vitamin A); mark scheme: 'Golden Rice contains vitamin A'.
findings.truth: Golden rice contains beta-carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A. Beta-carotene is a precursor, not vitamin A itself.
findings.evidence: settled biochemistry

findings.claim: Lines of defence cited as (B6.3b), vaccination as (B6.3c), antibiotics as (B6.3d).
findings.truth: B6.3b is types of disease, B6.3c is interactions between diseases and B6.3d is how communicable diseases spread. Non-specific defences are B6.3h; vaccines and medicines including antibiotics are B6.3j.
findings.evidence: spec B6.3 statement table

findings.claim: The whole exam tip is one sentence, 'A common mistake is saying antibiotics kill viruses - they do not.', and it carries no data-narration-id, while every other lesson in the unit has a full narrated tip (the manifest skips n21 for this lesson).
findings.truth: The tip looks truncated or partly overwritten. Restoring it means authoring new text and a narration block, which is an editorial call and would ripple into narration, so it is not edited here. Recommendation: rewrite the tip to the length of the other seven and re-narrate lesson 7.
findings.evidence: narration_manifest length 24 matches ids n1-n20 and n22-n25; n21 is absent

findings.claim: Lesson-to-paper mapping and coverage of B4-B6.
findings.truth: Mapping is correct: all eight lessons sit in Paper 2 (Foundation) / Paper 8 (Higher), which assess B4-B6 with B1-B3 as assumed knowledge and CS7 practical skills (PAGs B1-B5). L1 and L2 cover B4.1, L3 covers B5.1, L4 covers B5.2, L5 covers B6.1, L6 covers B6.2, L7 covers B6.3a-k and L8 covers B6.3l-r. Coverage gaps, none of which can be closed without new authoring and re-narration: (a) B5.2b classification and molecular phylogenetics is examined in L4 practice [4] and knowledge check [3] but is taught nowhere in the article text; (b) B6.2c the main steps of genetic engineering is examined seven times in L6 but never taught in the article; (c) B6.3f plant diseases (tobacco mosaic virus, barley powdery mildew, crown gall) are absent from the unit, as is any plant element of B6.3d and B6.3e; (d) B6.3e detection of the antigen, DNA testing and visual identification are absent; (e) B6.3g platelets are never mentioned; (f) B6.3j antivirals and antiseptics are never named; (g) B5.1d, that most variants have no effect on the phenotype, is absent. Recommendation: add short paragraphs for (a), (b), (c) and (e) first, as each is directly examinable.
findings.evidence: spec content overview for Paper 2 / Paper 8; statement-by-statement check of B4.1, B5.1, B5.2, B6.1, B6.2 and B6.3 against the eight lessons

findings.claim: After the F17 tier tags, four of the five knowledge checks in L6 are Higher Tier only, leaving Foundation students one item (selective breeding).
findings.truth: The tags are correct, but the balance is not. Recommendation: author three replacement Foundation items on B6.2a selective breeding, B6.2b what genetic engineering is, and B6.2d benefits and risks of gene technology, and keep the Higher four as extension.
findings.evidence: spec bold file B6.2; B6.2a, B6.2b and B6.2d are all both-tier

findings.claim: Most of L6 is fertilisers, pesticides, biological control, integrated pest management, hydroponics, insect farming, agroforestry and permaculture.
findings.truth: None of that is in this specification. B6.2 is only selective breeding, what genetic engineering is, its main steps (Higher) and the benefits and risks of gene technology. The material is not wrong, so it is left in place, but the two statements that are examinable get one paragraph between them. Recommendation: rebalance when L6 is next revised.
findings.evidence: spec B6.2 statement table; grep of the spec returns no match for pesticide as a content term, biological control, hydroponic or crop rotation

findings.claim: Each chromosome carries hundreds of genes
findings.truth: Human chromosomes carry hundreds to about two thousand genes each, so 'hundreds' understates it. Not mark-affecting at GCSE, so not edited.
findings.evidence: settled genetics

summary: Eight lessons checked against OCR Gateway Combined Science A, Paper 2 / Paper 8 (B4-B6). No science was badly wrong in the article text, but the specification references are: seventeen statement codes are shifted or point at codes that do not exist (B4.2b, B5.2f, B6.1d), three exam tips invent an 8-mark question style that these 60-mark papers do not have, two paragraphs claim the specification requires content it never mentions (eutrophication, food miles), one knowledge check has two correct answers, and the only Higher-tier statement in B4-B6 (B6.2c, genetic engineering steps) is tested seven times in lesson 6 with no tier flag.
